content:
Dear Lean community (especially Lean educators),

Software Foundations is a series of textbooks on formal proof and foundations of programming languages, all formalized in Rocq. After thinking about it for years, we have finally gathered enough organizational energy to start seriously translating Software Foundations to Lean. We have been working on the translation for a couple of months now and plan to have it ready for use in Fall courses at Penn and elsewhere.

We've kept the initial team very small, but we are ready now to add a few people to the translation effort.  If you are interested in joining in, could you please drop me an email with a few details about yourself...

  • your level of experience in Lean (Rocq experience useful but not required),
  • your background in either teaching or expository writing,
  • your availability (hours per week, starting when) between now and late August, and
  • any specific interests or perspectives you might bring to the effort?

Since the translation is still in an early stage, we'd especially love to work with people who want to use SF-in-Lean in their own teaching and who would therefore bring both pedagogical background and capacity to devote nontrivial effort over the coming weeks. We'll also need a larger group of alpha-testers a bit later in the summer.

Thank you!

- Benjamin
Discussion thread here: #Lean for teaching > Discussion: SF in Lean: Call for Contributions
